study.title: Shared and distinct brain activation patterns of acupoints HT7, ST36, and KI4: a task-based fMRI study
study.study_design: task-based fMRI study with between-subjects comparison of three acupoint groups; within-subject block design during acupuncture
study.randomization: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three stimulation orders—ST36 followed by KI4, ST36 followed by HT7, or KI4 followed by HT7—using computer-generated assignments in R (v4.0.5)
study.population: healthy, right-handed Han participants, aged 51–73 years (mean age ± SD: 60.67 ± 7.88); six males, 21 females; recruited from Shenzhen Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy, right-handed Han participants; aged 51–73 years
study.exclusion_criteria: Individuals with neurological, psychiatric, or medical conditions, a history of drug abuse, head trauma with loss of consciousness, premenopausal women, or a BMI < 18.5 or ≥24 or contraindications to high magnetic fields were excluded

arms.dropouts: Two participants were excluded from The HT7 group due to excessive head movement and severe pain
one participant was excluded from the KI4 group for excessive head movement

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or non-acupoint control group was included. Authors explicitly acknowledge this as a limitation: 'this study lacked a sham acupuncture or non-acupoint control group. Consequently, we cannot definitively attribute the observed brain responses solely to acupoint-specific effects, as distinct from general somatosensory stimulation or placebo effects.'

Coordinate space (MNI vs. Talairach) is not explicitly stated in the text. The study used DARTEL normalization to the MNI standard EPI template, so MNI is inferred but not confirmed for reported coordinates.

Precise peak MNI coordinates are only clearly readable for the conjunction result (left cerebellar crus II: -39, -69, -45 from Figure 3 caption). Coordinates for all other clusters are not provided in the main text; they may be in Supplementary Table S1 and Supplementary Figure S2 which are not available in this PDF.

Supplementary Table S1 is referenced for between-group comparisons of deactivated brain regions but is not included in the provided PDF. Supplementary Figure S1 shows participant flow. Supplementary Figure S2 shows specificity maps. Supplementary Figure S3 shows HT7/ST36 overlap. Supplementary Table S2 shows pain network overlap with HT7 (right cerebellar lobule IX and left cerebellar lobule VI).
Cluster sizes (in voxels) and precise T-statistics for each deactivation cluster are not reported in the main text. These may be in supplementary tables.
Expectancy, credibility, and treatment blinding/allocation guessing assessments are not reported or measured in this study. Authors state participants were not blinded and no sham control was used.

The MASS_R value for the ST36 group (Zusanli column, Table 1) is reported as '7.53 ± 50.63'. The SD of 50.63 appears anomalously large and may be a typographical error, but it is preserved as reported.

The study uses a within-subject design for each participant (each received two of three acupoints) but the fMRI analyses are performed as between-subjects comparisons. Exact sample sizes per arm reflect number of unique participants who received each acupoint, not unique individuals.
No behavioral or psychometric scales were used to directly validate functional interpretations derived from fMRI patterns. Authors acknowledge this as a limitation.

Figure 1B shows fullness and tingling deqi subscale scores across groups and sides with asterisks indicating P < 0.05, but exact numeric values (means, SDs) per subscale per arm are not reported in the text or a table; only narrative descriptions are extractable.
Figure 2 shows activation patterns for HT7, ST36, and KI4 with T-value color scale from -4 to -10, but cluster coordinates and statistics are not readable from figure captions in this PDF.
Figures 4 and 5 show MACM functional characterization bar charts and radar network diagrams, respectively, but precise voxel proportions in Figure 5 are not numerically extractable.

The paper describes 'activation' throughout but the Results section consistently reports 'deactivation' (negative BOLD responses). The contrast appears to be needle manipulation (on) minus baseline (off), with deactivations being the primary reported finding. No significant activations are reported in the main text.
The paper does not report filtering parameters (high-pass, low-pass), global signal regression, or explicit confound removal strategy beyond the six motion parameters.

The n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging of 51 is inferred by summing: 16 (HT7) + 19 (ST36) + 16 (KI4). Because each participant received two acupoints, the 51 represents scan-level analyses, not 51 unique individuals. Only 27 unique participants were enrolled.
